name: laravel
label: Laravel application
description: A door into a Laravel application that has benjaminledel/covey-laravel installed: the schema, read-only SQL and the application log behind the read token, tinker (PHP in the application's context) behind the write token.

schema.doc: the tables of the application's database (hidden tables left out); no params

columns.doc: the columns of one table with type, nullable and default; params: table

query.doc: ONE read-only SQL statement (SELECT/WITH/SHOW/EXPLAIN), rows capped; params: sql, bindings (optional array for ? placeholders), limit (optional). Anything that writes is refused here — that is tinker.

log_files.doc: the application's log files with size and modified time, newest first; no params. Only needed to pick one file for logs — a search does not need it.

logs.subject: logs
logs.doc: records from the application log, read from the end backwards, oldest first in the answer. A record is one log entry with its stack trace. params (all optional): grep (text, or a regex with regex: true; case-insensitive unless case_sensitive: true), level (list, e.g. "error,warning") or min_level, since / until ("2026-10-05 09:00:00" or "-2 hours"), tail (records, default 50), context (neighbouring records around each match, up to 5), lines (lines kept per record, the head of the trace), file (one file from log_files; without it every file, newest first). Secrets in the lines are redacted before you see them.

tinker.subject: tinker
tinker.doc: run PHP in the application's context, as `php artisan tinker` would (Eloquent, facades, jobs); params: code. This CHANGES things: say in one line what and why before you call it, and never call it for something query can answer.

prompt_doc: This Laravel application is reachable through six actions. Read first: schema and columns tell you the tables, query runs one SELECT with a row cap and strips columns the application hides, logs searches the application log by text, level and time and returns whole records with their stack trace. tinker is the only way to change anything and is governed separately — an organisation may require an approval for it, and an agent that only holds the read token does not have it at all. Prefer query over tinker for every question; use tinker for a change you were asked to make, name the record you touch, and read it back afterwards. For an error a person reports, start with logs: grep for what they saw or the request id, around the time they saw it, then open the code the trace names.
